definition: to mention, hint, or propose
example: She was hoping the waiter would *suggest* a good dish from the menu.

definition: appropriate or fitting; well-matched
example: That bright red dress is not *suitable* clothing for a funeral.

definition: to express in an abbreviated way
example: Since I did not have time to read the entire chapter, I asked my sister to *summarize* it for me.

definition: to call upon for specified action
example: My friend *summoned* me to her locker so she could show me her new book.

definition: to encourage or to uphold
example: Having known you for many years, I *support* your decision to run for president.

definition: assumed to be true; hypothetical
example: Jerry, a *supposed* master chef, baked a birthday cake that was inedible.

definition: to go beyond
example: She has *surpassed* her original weight lifting goal of 250 pounds and can now easily lift 300 pounds.

definition: taken aback; feeling wonder or astonishment
example: I was pleasantly *surprised* to discover that my roommate had unloaded the dishwasher.

definition: enclosed on all sides; encircled
example: The thief had to admit defeat when he found that the police had *surrounded* him.

definition: the act of continuing to live or exist, especially under hard conditions
example: The company’s *survival* will depend on whether it can avoid bankruptcy.

definition: to stay alive
example: The stranded hikers were able to *survive* by eating berries and grass for several days.

definition: to support, hold, or bear up from below
example: A bridge can *sustain* a lot of weight.

definition: to put on the same timetable
example: The family *synchronized* their watches and agreed to meet back at the front of the amusement park at noon.

definition: a piece of work assigned to someone
example: My *task* at the restaurant is to cut all fruits and vegetables.

definition: a method for accomplishing a task
example: My *techniques* for baking bread are slightly unusual, but work quite well.

definition: related to science and industry
example: *Technological* innovations such as the vacuum and washing machine have made housework much easier.

definition: to take care of or look after
example: I am happy to *tend* to your plants while you are away on vacation.

definition: leaning toward a particular kind of thought or action
example: He has a *tendency* to want to walk the longer way home from school because it is a habit.

definition: the action of stretching until stiff
example: The *tension* on the rope was so tight that he was afraid it would snap at any minute.

definition: made or done as a trial, experiment, or attempt; experimental; unsure; uncertain
example: These plans are *tentative*; we may change them at a later date.

definition: a word or group of words used to represent something
example: The *term* “gridlock” refers to a traffic jam in which cars cannot move.

definition: distressing; extremely bad
example: We had a *terrible* time reaching the log cabin; we must have gotten lost ten times!

definition: an idea that explains a phenomenon or occurrence
example: The scientist’s *theory* explained why the temperature had risen in the last few years.

definition: an indication that something bad is about to happen
example: The controversial political leader received daily *threats* to his life.

definition: a subject of study or discussion
example: The historian’s favorite *topic* of conversation was the Trojan War.

definition: a vehicle used to haul equipment, usually on a farm
example: The farmer used the *tractor* to carry many of his other machines to and from the fields.

definition: an established convention or activity
example: It is a *tradition* for my family to sit and watch “A Christmas Story” every Christmas while I complain about it.

definition: based on an established custom or convention
example: In a *traditional* Italian meal, pasta is always served.

definition: to move across something
example: She *transferred* the hot egg from one hand to the other so she wouldn’t burn herself.

definition: to change in form or appearance
example: At 10:00 P.M. on Friday night, we will *transform* the dorm room into a rocking party venue!

definition: a change from one place or state to another
example: Changing jobs is always a difficult *transition*.

definition: to move a sound or signal from one place to another
example: Cellular towers help to *transmit* signals from one phone to another.

definition: fine or sheer; able to see through
example: The wall was so *transparent* that many thought it was a window.

definition: to move something from one place to another
example: It was hard to *transport* the grand piano up several flights of stairs, but we did it.

definition: the general course or prevailing tendency
example: Rose gold watches are a popular jewelry *trend* today.

definition: kind or class
example: There are many *types* of dogs, but the Irish Setter is my favorite.

definition: conforming to regular behavior
example: In Seattle, it *typically* rains every day.

definition: having the agreement or support of all
example: A *unanimous* verdict could not be reached, as one jury member refused to vote “guilty.”

definition: extremely wrong or bad; without a moral guide
example: The actions of the criminal were so *unconscionable* that not even his lawyer could come up with a good reason to let him go free.

definition: to impair; to subvert; to weaken
example: The children’s adamant refusal to learn French considerably *undermines* their teacher’s efforts.

definition: below
example: I keep my slippers *underneath* my bed.

definition: to underline; to emphasize
example: Harold’s terrible hunger *underscores* the importance of remembering to eat.

definition: to comprehend the meaning of
example: The student did not *understand* the complex mathematical equation.

definition: an agreement between two parties
example: He did not have a good *understanding* of calculus and therefore struggled on the AP Exam.

definition: not favored by fortune; unlucky
example: It is *unfortunate* timing that your senior prom and your grandmother’s 80th birthday party are on the same day.

definition: tending to bring together or unite
example: Attending sports events can have a *unifying* effect on a community.

definition: one of a kind; having no equal
example: New York City is a *unique* place—there is no place like it in the entire world.

definition: affecting or concerning all; concerning the entire universe
example: It is a *universal* truth that what goes up must come down.

definition: not like; different from
example: *Unlike* New York, Los Angeles is sunny and warm for most of the year.

definition: unable to be predicted or foreseen
example: Life as a musician is *unpredictable*—you never know when you’ll get your next gig.

definition: not ordinary or common
example: Marge’s blue hair gave her an *unusual* appearance.

definition: helpful or serviceable
example: A compass is a *useful* tool for backpacking in the wild.

definition: regularly or habitually; most of the time
example: She *usually* eats toast for breakfast, but today she had pancakes.

definition: a fictional place where everything is good
example: A book lover might consider a well-stocked library to be her *utopia*.

definition: possessing worth, use, or importance
example: Gold is particularly *valuable* during times of economic uncertainty.

definition: the worth or importance of an object
example: He *valued* the scarf he made for a charity event at $20.

definition: of different kinds
example: The peacock’s feathers are composed of *various* colors.

definition: to change or be different
example: The quality of education in this country *varies* from school to school.

definition: truthfulness
example: The *veracity* of the story of young George Washington chopping down the cherry tree is questioned by serious historians.

definition: to confirm the truth of an action
example: Makalya will *verify* that her schedule is correct so that she won’t be late for her soccer game.

definition: in a direction from top to bottom
example: The running course is flat, except for a *vertical* ascent in the last mile.

definition: capable of living
example: The plans for the skyscraper are *viable*; construction will begin immediately.

definition: to compete
example: Sheryl *vied* with her best friend for a promotion.

definition: constantly alert; watchful; wary
example: The *vigilant* father guarded the door of the living room to keep the children from seeing the Easter Bunny at work.

definition: for the most part; almost entirely
example: In 1983, Tom Cruise was *virtually* unknown outside his small group of friends.

definition: able to be seen
example: On a clear day, Mount Hood is *visible* from most locations in Portland.

definition: pertaining to seeing
example: The film had great *visual* effects, such as fireballs and flying people.

definition: having free will
example: He made a *voluntary* decision to confess, hoping that his cooperation would reduce his punishment.

definition: a person who does work without getting paid
example: The *volunteer* collected samples for the scientists because she needed the experience even though she would not be paid.

definition: to fail to use; to use for no good reason
example: We *waste* electricity every time we leave a lamp on in an unoccupied room.

definition: to grow or advance
example: Chris will *wax* his surfboard to keep it water-repellant.

definition: well-being, happiness, or health
example: The country provided free health coverage for the *welfare* of its citizens.

definition: while on the contrary
example: I like chocolate cake, *whereas* my brother prefers lemon cake.

definition: determined by chance or impulse
example: The author turned out to be just as *whimsical* as the playful and amusing character in her book.

definition: clever; deceptive
example: The *wily* squirrel was always thinking of sneaky ways to get food from the “squirrel-proof” bird feeder.

definition: to shrink
example: The flower *withered* and died when the plant was left without water for a month.

definition: a fear of people from other countries
example: Despite his *xenophobia*, he packed his bags, got on the plane, and started to explore different countries.

definition: to desire strongly
example: Audrey *yearned* to get back all her favorite baby toys her mom had donated to others.

definition: to give or supply
example: The tomato plant will *yield* a huge number of tomatoes.

definition: to join together
example: Two oxen were *yoked* together and hooked up to pull the plow.

definition: marked by an active interest or enthusiasm
example: The lifelong fan was so *zealous* about getting a ticket to the show that she stayed up all night and slept in the rain just to purchase one.

definition: the time at which something is most powerful
example: Some suspect that musician is at the *zenith* of his musical career, and all the songs he produces in the future will be worse than what he has previously produced.

definition: characterized by sharp turns in different directions
example: The car proceeded in a *zigzag* fashion, attempting to avoid the cops.
